title: Analytification and closed direct image
statement:
Let $i:X\hookrightarrow Y$ be a closed immersion of separated finite-type smooth schemes over $\mathbf C$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $i^{\mathrm{an}}:X^{\mathrm{an}}\hookrightarrow Y^{\mathrm{an}}$ be the induced closed holomorphic embedding [lem-sfb-smooth-analytification-cotangent]. Write $\pi_X,\pi_Y$ for the analytification maps, and $a_E:E\to\pi_*E^{\mathrm{an}}$ for $s\mapsto1\otimes s$. For every coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $F$ [pqf-def-coherent], the canonical tensor map and the identification of direct-image sections give a canonical isomorphism of analytic $\mathcal O_{Y^{\mathrm{an}}}$-modules
$$ (i_*F)^{\mathrm{an}}\;\cong\;i^{\mathrm{an}}_*F^{\mathrm{an}}. $$
It sends a local tensor $h\otimes s$ to $h|_{X^{\mathrm{an}}}\otimes s$ and, after applying $\pi_{Y,*}$, identifies $a_{i_*F}$ with $i_*a_F$, using $i_*\pi_{X,*}=\pi_{Y,*}i^{\mathrm{an}}_*$.

source.place: WANTED: Serre, Géométrie algébrique et géométrie analytique, §10 Prop.11(i), printed p.18; stalk calculation for a closed immersion.

proof.text: Construct $\alpha:(i_*F)^{\mathrm{an}}\to i^{\mathrm{an}}_*F^{\mathrm{an}}$ on inverse-image representatives. For $U\subseteq Y$ open, $s\in(i_*F)(U)=F(i^{-1}U)$ and analytic $W\subseteq\pi_Y^{-1}U$, pull $s$ to $1\otimes s$ on $\pi_X^{-1}(i^{-1}U)$ and restrict to $(i^{\mathrm{an}})^{-1}W$. Pair this section with $h\in\mathcal O_{Y^{\mathrm{an}}}(W)$ by multiplication by $h|_{(i^{\mathrm{an}})^{-1}W}$. The square of analytification maps commutes: both paths send a complex point to its underlying algebraic point and a regular function to its holomorphic evaluation. Thus the indicated domains agree. Refining an inverse-image representative restricts both entries, so the rule is well defined, additive in both variables and balanced over $\pi_Y^{-1}\mathcal O_Y$; multiplication by a regular function gives the same product on both sides. The inverse-image colimit and the sheafifications defining inverse image and tensor therefore give the required module map. Its formula is $h\otimes s\mapsto h|_{X^{\mathrm{an}}}\otimes s$.

For any algebraic module $E$ and analytic point $z$ of its scheme $T$, the tensor-stalk isomorphism, applied over the ringed space $(T^{\mathrm{an}},\pi_T^{-1}\mathcal O_T)$, and the inverse-image stalk isomorphism identify
$$(E^{\mathrm{an}})_z=\mathcal O_{T^{\mathrm{an}},z}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{T,\pi_T(z)}}E_{\pi_T(z)}.$$
The scalar action agrees because multiplication in the inverse-image module is multiplication of representatives on a common open; the inverse-image stalk comparison sends a pulled-back section germ to its original germ. At $y=i^{\mathrm{an}}(x)$, write $x_0=\pi_X(x)$, $y_0=i(x_0)$, $M=F_{x_0}$ and put $A=\mathcal O_{Y,y_0}$, $R=\mathcal O_{X,x_0}$, $B=\mathcal O_{Y^{\mathrm{an}},y}$, $D=\mathcal O_{X^{\mathrm{an}},x}$. The algebraic closed-pushforward stalk theorem identifies $(i_*F)_{y_0}$ with $M$ as an $A$-module. The topological closed-pushforward theorem identifies $(i^{\mathrm{an}}_*F^{\mathrm{an}})_y$ with $(F^{\mathrm{an}})_x$; its germ map is $B$-linear through $B\to D$, since restriction of a product is the product of restrictions. Consequently the source and target stalks of $\alpha$ are $B\otimes_A M$ and $D\otimes_R M$, and the section formula from step 1 identifies $\alpha_y$ with $b\otimes m\mapsto\bar b\otimes m$.

source.place: Tags 01CB (modules.tex, lemma-stalk-tensor-product), 008H (lemma-stalk-pullback), 008X (module action on inverse image), 00AE (lemma-stalks-closed-pushforward).

proof.text:
The algebraic map $A\to R$ is surjective: a germ of an $\mathcal O_X$-section lifts locally through the surjective sheaf map in the definition of closed immersion. With $I$ its kernel, $R=A/I$. The local analytic ideal theorem gives $D=B/IB$ through the actual restriction map. The inverse to the stalk map in step 2 is
$$(B/IB)\otimes_{A/I}M\longrightarrow B\otimes_A M,\qquad[b]\otimes m\longmapsto b\otimes m.$$
This is independent of the lift of $[b]$: each difference $b'a$ with $a\in I$ contributes $b'a\otimes m=b'\otimes am=0$. It is balanced over $A/I$ by lifting a scalar to $A$ and using the tensor balancing relation; different scalar lifts differ by $I$ and act by zero on $M$. Both composites fix pure tensors and hence every tensor. Thus $\alpha_y$ is invertible at every point in the analytic closed image.

source.place: Serre, §6 Proposition 4 and §10 Proposition 11 (printed pp.10–11,18); the displayed inverse and its balancing are elementary tensor algebra. (External source WANTED locally.)

proof.text: If $y\notin i^{\mathrm{an}}(X^{\mathrm{an}})$, then $\pi_Y(y)\notin i(X)$. Indeed, if a complex point of $Y$ has underlying point in the closed subscheme, the defining ideal maps to zero in its residue field and therefore in $\mathbf C$; the complex point factors uniquely through $X$, giving an analytic preimage. The algebraic closed-pushforward stalk theorem now gives $(i_*F)_{\pi_Y(y)}=0$. The tensor and inverse-image stalk comparisons of step 2 make $((i_*F)^{\mathrm{an}})_y=\mathcal O_{Y^{\mathrm{an}},y}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{Y,\pi_Y(y)}}0=0$. The topological closed-pushforward stalk theorem also gives $(i^{\mathrm{an}}_*F^{\mathrm{an}})_y=0$. Hence $\alpha_y$ is an isomorphism off the closed image as well.

source.place: Tags 00AE (lemma-stalks-closed-pushforward), 01CB (modules.tex, lemma-stalk-tensor-product), 008H (lemma-stalk-pullback); affine quotient clause of closed immersion.

proof.text: The criterion that a sheaf map is an isomorphism exactly when all stalk maps are bijective proves $\alpha$ invertible. Its inverse preserves addition and scalar multiplication by cancelling the corresponding identities through the bijective linear maps $\alpha_U$, so it is an analytic module isomorphism. Finally, on any algebraic open $U\subseteq Y$ and $s\in F(i^{-1}U)$, the composite $\pi_{Y,*}(\alpha)\,a_{i_*F}$ sends $s$ first to $1\otimes s$ and then to $1|_{X^{\mathrm{an}}}\otimes s=1\otimes s$. This is exactly $(i_*a_F)_U(s)$. The direct-image composition identification is literal on sections, since both sides evaluate $F^{\mathrm{an}}$ on $\pi_X^{-1}(i^{-1}U)=(i^{\mathrm{an}})^{-1}(\pi_Y^{-1}U)$, with the same restrictions. This proves the required compatibility with the specified canonical maps, not merely existence of an abstract isomorphism.
